exercises.title: U3 听力·对话 Talking about a Hero
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Lily: I just finished reading about Ernest Shackleton. What an amazing explorer!
Tom: I've heard of him. He tried to cross Antarctica, didn't he?
Lily: Yes, but his ship got stuck in the ice and was crushed before it sank.
Tom: So he never reached the land he planned to cross?
Lily: No, he failed to reach his goal. But the wonderful thing is that he brought every man home alive.
Tom: Every single one? After the ship was lost?
Lily: That's right. They lived on the ice for almost two years. People remember him for his leadership, not for winning.
Tom: Now I really want to read that book too.
exercises.translation_cn: Lily 刚读完关于沙克尔顿的书,说他是了不起的探险家;Tom 知道他想横穿南极;Lily 说他的船被冰困住、压碎后沉没,目标没达成,但了不起的是把全员活着带回;船在冰上漂了近两年;人们记住他是因为领导力而非成功;Tom 也想读这本书。

options: For his leadership rather than for winning.

exercises.title: U3 听力·独白 A Radio Report from the Ice
exercises.speaker: uk_male
transcript: Good evening. Tonight we look back at one of the greatest survival stories in history. In 1915 a ship became trapped in the frozen sea near Antarctica. For many months the crew waited in the freezing dark, hoping the ice would let them go. Instead, the moving ice crushed the wooden ship, and the men were left alone with only three small boats. They camped on the ice and drifted slowly north, never giving up hope of rescue. Their courage in the face of such danger still amazes us today.
exercises.translation_cn: 晚间节目回顾历史上最伟大的生还故事之一:1915年一艘船被困在南极附近结冰的海域;船员们在极冷的黑暗中等待数月,盼冰松开;然而移动的冰压碎了木船,只剩三条小艇;他们在冰上扎营、缓缓向北漂,从未放弃获救的希望;他们面对危险的勇气至今令人惊叹。

options: In the frozen sea near Antarctica.

questions.stem: What finally happened to the ship?
options: It was burned by the crew.

questions.stem: What did the men do after losing the ship?
options: They swam to the nearest city.
They camped on the ice and drifted north.

questions.stem: What does the speaker admire about the men?

exercises.title: U3 听力·对话 Planning a Polar Trip
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Anna: I'd love to join a polar expedition one day. Do you think I could?
Ben: Maybe, but it takes a lot of planning. You can't just set out.
Anna: What do I need to learn first?
Ben: You should learn to read maps and to understand the weather. Storms can appear without warning.
Anna: That sounds frightening. How do explorers stay warm?
Ben: They use special clothing and strong tents made for the cold. And modern teams carry radios.
Anna: So they can call for rescue if something goes wrong?
Ben: Exactly. But careful planning still matters as much as courage. You should train for months before you go.
exercises.translation_cn: Anna 想有朝一日参加极地探险,问能否做到;Ben 说可能,但需要大量准备,不能贸然出发;Anna 问先学什么;Ben 说要会看地图、懂天气,因为风暴会突然来;探险者靠特制衣物和耐寒帐篷保暖,现代队伍还带无线电;Anna 问出事能否求救;Ben 说能,但谨慎规划与勇气同样重要,出发前要训练数月。

options: Learn to read maps and understand the weather.

questions.stem: Why is the weather so important?
options: It is always sunny at the poles.

questions.stem: How do modern teams keep safe?
options: They use warm gear and carry radios.

questions.stem: What matters as much as courage, according to Ben?

exercises.title: U3 听力·独白 My First Voyage
exercises.speaker: uk_male
transcript: When I first went to sea, I was a young sailor who knew almost nothing about ships. On my second day a storm rose, and the waves looked as high as mountains. Each time the ship dived into the deep water between the waves, I was sure we would never come up again. I was so frightened that I promised to go straight home to my father and never sail again. But the next morning the wind died away and the sea became calm and beautiful. My fear faded as quickly as the storm, and soon I almost forgot all the promises I had made.
exercises.translation_cn: 我初次出海时是个对船几乎一无所知的年轻水手;第二天起了风暴,浪高如山;每当船扎进浪谷,我都以为再也起不来了;我吓得发誓要直接回家找父亲、再也不出海;但第二天早上风停了,海变得平静又美丽;我的恐惧随风暴一样迅速消退,很快就几乎忘了所有的誓言。

options: To go home and never sail again.

options: It faded as the sea grew calm.

exercises.title: U3 听力·对话 A Night at Camp
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Sam: It's freezing tonight. I can hardly feel my hands.
Kate: Keep moving, then. If we sit still too long, we'll get too cold.
Sam: I know. How far is it to the station now?
Kate: About sixty kilometres, over the mountains. No one has crossed here on foot before.
Sam: And we have no tent. We can't really stop to sleep, can we?
Kate: No. If we fall asleep in this cold, we might never wake up.
Sam: Then let's keep marching. Thinking of the others waiting for us helps me go on.
Kate: Same for me. Come on, the sooner we reach help, the sooner we can save them.
exercises.translation_cn: Sam 说今夜极冷,手都快没知觉;Kate 让他保持活动,坐太久会冻坏;Sam 问到站点还有多远;Kate 说约六十公里、要翻山,此前无人徒步穿越;Sam 说他们没帐篷,不能真正停下睡觉;Kate 说不能,在这种冷里睡着可能再也醒不来;Sam 说那就继续行进,想到等待的伙伴就有动力;Kate 也一样,越快求到援助,越快能去救他们。

exercises.title: U3 听力·独白 Why We Explore
exercises.speaker: uk_male
transcript: In this documentary we ask a simple question: why do people explore? Long ago, our ancestors wondered what lay beyond the distant hills and on the other side of the sky. That same wonder still moves us today. Some explorers want to gain knowledge and understand how the world works. Others simply wish to be the first to stand where no one has stood before. A few set out to test how much hardship they can bear. Exploring is rarely safe, yet people have never been willing to stay still. As long as an unknown world remains, someone will always want to set out and discover it.
exercises.translation_cn: 这部纪录片问一个简单的问题:人为何探险?很久以前,祖先们好奇远山之外、天空另一边有什么;同样的好奇至今驱动着我们;有的探险者想获取知识、理解世界如何运转;有的只想成为第一个站到无人到过之地的人;少数人出发是为了测试自己能承受多少艰难;探险很少安全,但人类从不愿安于现状;只要还有未知世界,总会有人想出发去发现它。
